The dynamics between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy serve as the primary vehicle for exploring the novel's themes of social class and personal growth. Their initial conflict, rooted in pride and prejudice, illustrates the rigid barriers of societal expectations. As they move from disdain to mutual respect, their relationship demonstrates that true connection requires overcoming internal biases and external social pressures, thereby highlighting the transformative power of self-reflection and love.
